Q: C# Style Switch Expressions in C++ A:

He's asking about expressions, not statements. Closest thing in standard C++ right now is the ternary condition? if-true: if-false operator.

Q: Optimizing query with nested where clauses A:

This seems too long for a comment. My guess is that the or is killing the performance with the current index structure.

One possibility is to break the query into a union statement:

SELECT CALLID FROM CALLS
WHERE CALLS.USERID_OPENED_BY = 1 
union
SELECT CALLID FROM CALLS
WHERE CALLS.AREAID IN (1,2,3)
union 
SELECT CALLID FROM CALLS
WHERE CALLS.TYPEID IN (1,2,3)

Usually, I abhor this sort of change, but you can see if it improves the execution plan. Notice I used union here rather than union all to eliminate duplicates.

However, you say that this is not possible.

One other idea would be to combine the areas and types into the same reference table. This would reduce the number of indexes to two in the WHERE clause, perhaps making the join more optimal. Otherwise, can you train your users to just not select all three at the same time? Is this functionality really needed for the application?

Q: How do I get a value of datetime.today() in Python that is "time zone aware"? A:

Another method to construct a time zone-aware datetime object representing current time:

import datetime
import pytz

pytz.utc.localize(datetime.datetime.utcnow())

You can install pytz from PyPI by running:

pipenv install pytz

Q: Code to create a pie chart with plotly previously worked but now I keep getting 'unexpected symbol' A:

The problem is here:

labels=~factor(Bleibt genug Zeit für Freizeit?)

To reference a column name that isn't a valid R identifier (spaces, punctuation, umlauts in awkward spots, ?, etc.), you need to wrap it in backticks

That's a column name with spaces, special characters, and a ? in it. R's parser sees Bleibt, then hits a space and the next token genug, and stops parsing. That's why you see "unexpected symbol".

This code will work:

plotly::plot_ly(data = surveyresponses_Freizeit_Bachelor_count,
                values = ~n,
                labels = ~factor(`Bleibt genug Zeit für Freizeit?`),
                marker = list(colors = c("green", "orange", "blue")),
                type = "pie") %>%
  layout(title = "Bleibt genug Zeit für Freizeit im Bachelor?")

Q: MySQL query: GROUP BY - get specific row (not always the first one) A:

There is a way to do this without a correlated subquery:

SELECT id, sort, isum.cnt
FROM images i join
     (select i.album_id, count(*) as cnt
      from images
     ) isum
     on i.album_id = isum.album_id
WHERE user_id = 15 and
      sort = 0

I generally prefer to have all my tables listed in the FROM clause. However, some databases will optimize the correlated subquery better than this form, when there is an index on album_id.

Also, I renamed the third field from count to cnt. It is a very, very bad idea to name columns after SQL reserved words, unless you really have to.

And, finally, most other dialects of SQL support the window function. So, if you change databases, you can do something like

select id, sort, count(*) over (partition by album_id)
from images
where user_id = 15 and
      sort = 0

Q: Cursor positioning does not work as expected in QPlainTextEdit in python A:

When I try to use

self.result_text.moveCursor(self.cursor.atEnd())
self.result_text.moveCursor(self.cursor.atStart())

then I raises error because atEnd() and atStart() gives value True/False
but function moveCursor() expects something different.

TypeError: moveCursor(self, operation: QTextCursor.MoveOperation, mode: QTextCursor.MoveMode = QTextCursor.MoveAnchor): 
argument 1 has unexpected type 'bool'

Doc: atEnd()

Returns true if the cursor is at the end of the document; otherwise returns false.

Doc: atStart()

Returns true if the cursor is at the start of the document; otherwise returns false.

Correct use is (with QTextCursor.MoveOperation)

from PyQt6.QtGui import QTextCursor

self.result_text.moveCursor(QTextCursor.MoveOperation.End)
self.result_text.moveCursor(QTextCursor.MoveOperation.Start)

Tested on Linux Mint 22 (based on Ubuntu 24.04), Python 3.13, PyQt 6.11

Full working code for tests:

import sys
from PyQt6.QtWidgets import QApplication, QWidget, QVBoxLayout, QPlainTextEdit
from PyQt6.QtGui import QTextCursor

from PyQt6.QtCore import PYQT_VERSION_STR, QT_VERSION_STR

print("PyQt:", PYQT_VERSION_STR)
print("Qt:", QT_VERSION_STR)


class Window(QWidget):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()

        self.result_text = QPlainTextEdit()
        # self.result_text.setPlainText("Hello world")

        self.cursor = self.result_text.textCursor()

        text = self.result_text.toPlainText()
        print(text)

        self.test()

        layout = QVBoxLayout()
        layout.addWidget(self.result_text)
        self.setLayout(layout)

    def test(self):
        self.result_text = QPlainTextEdit()
        self.cursor = self.result_text.textCursor()
        print(self.result_text.toPlainText())
        print("---")

        self.result_text.insertPlainText("1\n")
        print(self.result_text.toPlainText())
        print("---")

        #    '1\n'

        self.result_text.insertPlainText("2\n")
        print(self.result_text.toPlainText())
        print("---")

        #    '1\n2\n'

        # self.result_text.moveCursor(self.cursor.atEnd())  # it raises Error
        self.result_text.moveCursor(QTextCursor.MoveOperation.End)  # it works
        # self.cursor.movePosition(QTextCursor.MoveOperation.End)  # it needs  `setTextCursor()` to work
        # self.result_text.setTextCursor(self.cursor)


        self.result_text.insertPlainText("3\n")
        print(self.result_text.toPlainText())
        print("---")

        #    '3\n1\n2\n'

        # Now the result seem to enter the text at the start although I set the cursor position at the end.

        # self.result_text.moveCursor(self.cursor.atStart())  # it raises Error
        self.result_text.moveCursor(QTextCursor.MoveOperation.Start)  # it works
        # self.cursor.movePosition(QTextCursor.MoveOperation.Start)  # it needs  `setTextCursor()` to work
        # self.result_text.setTextCursor(self.cursor)

        self.result_text.insertPlainText("4\n")
        print(self.result_text.toPlainText())
        print("---")

        #    '3\n4\n1\n2\n'

        # If I set the cursor position at the start it append the new text after the previous one! If I keep inserting text it is appended after the previous one.

        self.result_text.insertPlainText(" 5 ")
        print(self.result_text.toPlainText())
        print("---")

        #    '3\n4\n 5 1\n2\n'

        self.result_text.insertPlainText(" 6 ")
        print(self.result_text.toPlainText())
        print("---")

        #    '3\n4\n 5 6 1\n2\n'

        print("position:", self.cursor.position())

        #    14

        print("len:", len(self.result_text.toPlainText()))


# --- main ---

app = QApplication(sys.argv)

window = Window()
window.show()

app.exec()
